transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-12
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Hannah Lee (Redwood AE), Marcus Patel (Redwood SE), Ivy Chen (Redwood CSM); Carlos Mendez (SierraNode CTO), Priya Rao (Platform Eng), Liam O'Neill (DevOps), Elena Park (Security), Samir Gupta (Product)
Summary: Technical sync for SierraNode marketplace listing plus on-prem helm chart packaging and KMS/VPC integration. Discussed packaging artifacts, network preflight, quantization/runtime compat, helm values, and UAT plan.
Topics: marketplace listing checklist, helm chart layout, private deploy KMS handshake, ingress/NAT and firewall rules, billing/metering expectations, quantization artifacts, canary rollout plan for listing, docs links
Links referenced: https://redwood.example/docs/marketplace-onprem (deck), https://redwood.example/helm/sample-values.yaml, internal benchmark spreadsheet (shared via link in chat)

Transcript body:
[00:00] Hannah Lee: ok hey everyone thanks for making time, um today we want to run through packaging the helm chart for SierraNode's on-prem listing and make sure the KMS/VPC flow lines up with your security needs
[00:12] Carlos Mendez: thanks Hannah yeah we've got the team here, we want to avoid surprises during reviewer gate, last time packaging caused back and forth with helm hooks and preinstall jobs
[00:23] Marcus Patel: absolutely, and to call out upfront we have a recommended pattern that mirrors our private deployment reference - minimal preinstall, sidecar for telemetry, and an operator-friendly values structure. i'll share a sample values file after this
[00:38] Priya Rao: quick Q — will the marketplace listing require us to include entitlements or licensing hooks in the chart? or is that handled by the marketplace runtime?
[00:47] Hannah Lee: good question. for the Redwood hosted listing the entitlement is handled by the control plane, but for on-prem via marketplace we have two patterns: 1) marketplace just delivers the package and consumes a license token at install time, or 2) you bundle a small licensing init container. most partners go with the token approach. we can attach our packaging checklist link
[01:10] Liam O'Neill: ok that helps. network wise we have an egress-only policy out to a repository mirror and to KMS endpoints — how do you handle KMS handshake for air-gapped?
[01:20] Marcus Patel: for air-gapped we support a bring-your-own-kms shim where you provide a signed certificate bundle and we run the key wrap locally. it's a little manual: we exchange signed manifests. we'll need Elena's security team to validate the CSR process.
[01:34] Elena Park: yes, security will need the CSR + threat model, also need to confirm HSM compatibility — our cluster uses an HSM appliance that only allows specific key wrapping algorithms
[01:45] Marcus Patel: we can provide an HSM compatibility matrix, note that some runtime kernels expect AES-GCM or RSA-OAEP, we'll map that in the matrix. i'll add the compatibility doc to the ticket
[01:58] Samir Gupta: i want to flag quantization artifacts — SierraNode's model uses int8 quantization for cost; are there any runtime hooks Redwood requires in the chart to enable quantized kernels?
[02:08] Marcus Patel: yes, there are a couple flags. the runtime auto-selects kernels based on a node label and sequence length heuristics. we set a values flag: redwood.runtime.variant: quantized-int8 and then either mount the quantization artifact or point to OCI blob storage. for on-prem we recommend including the artifact in the package bundle when offline
[02:30] Priya Rao: how big are those artifacts usually? storage is a concern for some of our smaller customers
[02:35] Marcus Patel: ranges, typically 80–600MB depending on model; the larger LLMs get bigger. if you want dedupe we recommend an external blob repo that many tenants can pull from — saves space in image registry
[02:47] Hannah Lee: also want to surface listing metadata — the marketplace listing needs a reference architecture doc, a secure-install guide, and test vectors. we've got a template, Marcus will populate the sections relevant to helm and runtime
[02:58] Carlos Mendez: about network: our install is behind a NAT and we have strict inbound firewall rules. we need to confirm ingress expectations — does the chart require public ingress?
[03:09] Marcus Patel: no, it doesn't require public ingress. typical pattern is egress to Redwood control plane, with a reverse-proxy in your DMZ if you need remote support. for pure air-gapped, we do an offline activation. we'll outline both flows in the checklist
[03:23] Liam O'Neill: good. on the observability side, we need the metrics and traces to ship to our telemetry collector, not Redwood. is that configurable?
[03:31] Marcus Patel: yes, metrics exporter is sidecar-based and endpoint configurable. you can set redwood.telemetry.enabled=false and provide your prometheus scrape annotations in values.yaml
[03:43] Priya Rao: billing question — how is metering handled for an on-prem marketplace deployment? does Redwood provide metering hooks or do we need to bake that into the chart?
[03:53] Hannah Lee: Redwood provides optional metering hooks. For marketplace on-prem we give a metering sidecar that emits usage to a local collector and then you can either push to Redwood's metering endpoint, or you can proxy to your internal billing system. there's an example integration in the packaging docs
[04:06] Elena Park: security review — does Redwood sign the helm chart and artifacts? we need SHA and signature verification during CI
[04:14] Marcus Patel: yes, we support Cosign-signed artifacts. recommended flow: sign your helm chart and OCI images, include cosign verification in pre-install; we point to cosign public keys in the values/secret. i'll include an example pipeline snippet
[04:29] Samir Gupta: deployment strategy question — for marketplace listing rollouts, are canaries automated or manual? our product needs to support 10% canary then ramp
[04:38] Hannah Lee: the marketplace control plane supports canary routing if you opt into our rollout service. For on-prem packaged deployments, you can use the chart to set percentages and we support an admission webhook to assist gradual traffic shifting. we usually recommend a canary job + smoke tests in CI
[04:53] Liam O'Neill: about testing, can Redwood share a small synthetic load harness we can run in our staging so we can validate latency and memory?
[05:02] Marcus Patel: yes the engineering team has a small load harness and a perf profile for 512-token sequences; i'll provide a lightweight container you can run that exercises batch and concurrency scenarios
[05:15] Priya Rao: any special kernel or CUDA version constraints for GPU nodes we should be aware of?
[05:22] Marcus Patel: we support CUDA 11.8+ for our optimized kernels; if you use older drivers you may fall back to slower paths. also note mixed-precision kernels require nvcc compatible tooling. i'll add the exact driver matrix to the notes
[05:37] Carlos Mendez: reminds me, our security team also asked about audit logs and retention — can audit logs be shipped to our SIEM?
[05:45] Ivy Chen: yes, audit logs can be forwarded to your SIEM via syslog or HTTPS forwarding; retention policies are configurable in the values and at the control plane. we'll include recommended retention defaults for compliance teams
[05:58] Hannah Lee: okay who wants ownership of the UAT plan?
[06:02] Carlos Mendez: i'll own internal UAT coordination, Liam will run the deploy, and Samir will validate model quality post-deploy
[06:10] Samir Gupta: quick nit, transcription — one more thing on packaging: how do we handle hotfixes to quant artifacts? do we push new chart versions or patch in-place?
[06:18] Marcus Patel: we recommend patching artifacts via OCI blobs when possible; chart version can remain same if the artifact reference changes. for critical CVEs in runtime we issue a chart bump and a security advisory
[06:29] Priya Rao: ok next steps?
[06:33] Hannah Lee: recap: Marcus to share helm checklist + sample values + cosign pipeline snippet by 2026-08-19; Ivy to share security packing doc and SOC2 section by 2026-08-18; Liam to run staging deploy and attach logs by 2026-08-24; schedule week-of 2026-08-24 lab for KMS handshake with Elena and Ivy. we'll follow up with a short ticket that aggregates these artifacts
[06:50] Carlos Mendez: perfect thanks everyone
[06:53] Hannah Lee: thanks all, i'll drop links in the calendar act and follow up in Slack

Notes/observations: occasional transcription errors (names, acronyms), speaker overlaps near 04:00–05:00 were audible in the recording. All technical decisions were tentative pending the UAT run and security OK.
